title: Too many adds
body:
I used to love Study Bunny but these days I find it too distracting and impractical with the number of adverts that come up on the app.
If you lock your phone and go back to the app, you have to sit through a 10 second ad. If you pause the timer you also have to sit through a 10 second ad. 

If there was a paid version (one-off) which is ad free - I would be keen but for now I am back to timers on the clock app.

title: great app for staying on top of things!
body: i’ve been using this app for about a month now and it’s been great! i appreciate the simple and cohesive design and it helps me keep track of everything i need to do in the day. plus i like the fact that there’s a normal to do list and a schedule for timed tasks! have noticed some minor glitches (keyboard popping up when im done typing, focus music stops after 2 min) but not dealbreakers. definitely recommend to anyone who wants to stay on top of their to do list!

title: This app was great until I realized its predatory....
body: So this app is great! The interface is easy to work, and it really helps you keep your life together. On the other hand, the app markets itself towards people with ADHD/Autism who struggle with memory issues and executive dysfunction... so making your free trial for the year long subscription and not sending out reminders to cancel or about it "renewing" and charging you feels predatory. You know the clientele you are marketing towards, so it feels both purposeful and honesly kind of gross that you guys are marketing towards people with developmental delays and then doing stuff like that.
